mekayis.metin:
(دَسَتَ) الدَّالُ وَالسِّينُ وَالتَّاءُ لَيْسَ أَصْلًا، لِأَنَّ الدَّسْتَ الصَّحْرَاءُ وَهُوَ فَارِسِيٌّ مُعَرَّبٌ. قَالَ الْأَعْشَى:
قَدْ عَلِمَتْ فَارِسٌ وَحِمْيَرُ وَالْ ... أَعْرَابُ بِالدَّسْتِ أَيُّكُمْ نَزَلَا

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Borrowed from Persian دست (dast, literally “hand”) and دشت (dašt, “plain”).
g: a cushioning, carpeting, resting place, place of honor
pack of clothes, apparel, dress that accompanies a man of honour
a match of playing cards or chess or contest fighting etc.
hand, power, authority; lead in a game of cards etc.; pomp

kaikki_vikisozluk.e:
دست (form I)
# دَسَّتْ (dassat) /das.sat/: third-person feminine singular past active of دَسَّ (dassa)
# دُسَّتْ (dussat) /dus.sat/: third-person feminine singular past passive of دَسَّ (dassa)

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Yemeni Arabic and Egyptian Arabic of Cairo – in Alexandria and Libya one has دَزِّينَة (dazzīna, “dozen”), in the Gulf, Mekka and Aden دَرْزَن (darzan) –, a borrowing from Ottoman Turkish دسته (deste), from Persian دسته (dasta). Doublet of دَسْتَج (dastaj).
